subject: electrical-computer
audience: FE Electrical and Computer candidates and engineering students
title: The Gain-10 Loop That Only Reached 0.909
featured_title: THE GAIN-10 LOOP THAT ONLY REACHED 0.909

presentation.challenge: The forward gain was 10. The closed-loop output did not become 10 times the reference.

practice.primary_question: Why does a unity-feedback system with forward gain 10 have a closed-loop DC gain of only 10/11?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Using the forward-path gain as the closed-loop gain and ignoring the feedback denominator.

case_dna.target_misconception: In unity feedback, a forward gain of 10 means the output must be 10 times the reference.
case_dna.why_plausible: Students often read the forward block first and stop before reducing the feedback loop.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: For unity negative feedback, T = G/(1+G). With G = 10, T = 10/11 ≈ 0.909 and the unit-step steady-state error is 1/11 ≈ 0.091.
case_dna.corrected_model: Reduce the feedback loop before interpreting gain. For unity negative feedback, T(s)=G(s)/(1+G(s)) and E/R=1/(1+G).

problem_statement: A unity negative-feedback control loop has a constant forward-path gain G = 10. A review note says a 1.0 reference should produce an output of 10 because the controller gain is 10. In test, the output settles near 0.909. Diagnose the block-diagram error, calculate the closed-loop gain and steady-state error, and choose the change that reduces the error below 5%.
fixed_constraints: Forward path is a constant gain for this case

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The controller gain was 10. The output settled at 0.909.
gates.prompt: Which gain should be used to predict the output: forward-path gain or closed-loop gain?

options.label: Use T = G/(1+GH); with G=10 and H=1, T=10/11
options.reason: Negative feedback changes the input-output transfer function.

options.label: Use T = G = 10 because feedback only affects stability
options.reason: Feedback changes closed-loop gain as well as other response properties.

options.label: Use T = 1/G = 0.1
options.reason: The reciprocal of forward gain is not the closed-loop transfer function.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the steady output
gates.prompt: For a unit-step reference with G=10 and unity negative feedback, what output should the system approach?

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the closed-loop gain
gates.prompt: Calculate T = 10/(1+10). Enter the steady output for a unit-step input.
gates.success: T = 10/11 ≈ 0.909. The steady-state error is 1 - 0.909 ≈ 0.091, or 9.1%.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: The feedback algebra matches the measurement

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the control-loop review
report: C2. The feedback path is unity.
C3. Therefore the closed-loop gain is 10.

evidence_choices.label: T = 10/(1+10) = 10/11 ≈ 0.909
evidence_choices.reason: This is the closed-loop input-output gain.

correction.template: With unity negative feedback, the closed-loop gain is about {gain}, not 10.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Reduce steady-state error below 5%
gates.constraint: Keep unity negative feedback and a constant forward gain.

options.label: Increase forward gain to at least 20
options.reason: For a unit step, e_ss = 1/(1+G). G=20 gives 1/21 ≈ 4.76%.

options.label: Remove the feedback path
options.reason: That changes the system architecture and does not satisfy the stated constraint.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the unity-feedback rule
gates.prompt: A unity-feedback system has constant forward gain G=4. What is its closed-loop DC gain?

options.reason: That is 1/G, not the closed-loop gain.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the feedback reduction
gates.confirmation: I confirm that forward-path gain and closed-loop gain are not the same quantity in a feedback system.

items.label: What failed
items.value: The output was predicted from forward gain instead of closed-loop gain.

items.label: What was assumed
items.value: Feedback was treated as if it did not change input-output gain.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use T = G/(1+GH) before evaluating closed-loop response.

seo.seo_title: Unity Feedback Closed-Loop Gain: Why Gain 10 Becomes 0.909 | FE E-032
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Case E-032: a unity-feedback loop with forward gain 10 settles at 0.909, not 10. Calculate closed-loop gain and steady-state error.
seo.focus_keyphrase: unity feedback closed loop gain FE exam
seo.excerpt: A forward-path gain of 10 does not mean a closed-loop gain of 10. Reduce the feedback loop before predicting output.
seo.direct_answer: For unity negative feedback, the closed-loop transfer is T = G/(1+G). With G=10, T=10/11≈0.909. A unit-step input therefore produces about 0.909 output and 9.1% steady-state error.
